chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr [from Ubayd ibn Zurara], who said:

It reached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) concerning a man that he was consuming usury (riba) and he called it 'al-liba' (milk), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enables me [over him], I will strike his neck.'

key_terms.اللِّبَأَ: Milk (a specific term used to describe the usurious gain in this context)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a man who consumes usury but calls it milk?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) responded to a man who consumed usury but renamed it 'al-liba' (milk) to evade prohibition, declaring he would strike his neck if given power. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ghish* (deception) and the substantive reality of the act over its nominal label, reinforcing the severity of riba as a major sin. The phrase 'strike his neck' signifies a decisive judicial execution or severe corporal punishment, reflecting the Imam's authority in enforcing divine law against those who rationalize the forbidden.
